page.layout: One page of running text in a single column; running head at the top; a catchword-like word "mis" at the foot right, which is the end of a split word, not a catchword. No margin notes, no footnotes.

main_text.p: gratis qui beneficium accepit, reddere non potuit. In votis quidem esset, si in fatis & viribus.

En itaque, ô Consul, qua tua est humanitas Ampl. Tuam eum permittas jam, ea qua par observantia, compellare, quem Tibi natalis soli jus, quem primi amoris dulcis memoria, quem studiorum olim jucunda societas, quem deniq; animi grati ad remunerandum obligata propensio obstrinxit.

At vero quid feram ego Sineta Mnemoni? quid retribuā Evergeta olim meo? Manibus meis hauste aquam; In censu meo literario aliud donum offerendū cum jam non occurrat, en Munusculum literarium, fortè satis levidense, (quod quasi tamen Tibi ne fordeat) fero.

At inquies: Reipub. ego deploratissimis hīs temporibus mihi commissā, inter tot difficultates, turbas & pericula, operam & curam impendo: mihi quid cum natura mysteriis? quid cum Physicorum Musis philosophicis? Curia mea alias curas, difficilia hæc tempora alia postulant studia.
Scio equidem, quo splendidior est & divinior Reipub. administratio, eo ipsam solere laboriosiorem & difficiliorem esse, quippe cui communis humani generis hostis diabolus cumpri-mis

page.notes: The text runs to the foot of the page with the last word split ("cumpri-" / "mis"); the "mis" is printed at the bottom right. Some words are doubtful: "Ampl." and "Sineta Mnemoni" and "Evergeta" are proper names I read as printed; "quasi" and "quod quasi" are read with [?] in mind but the reading is reasonably clear. "Reipub.ego" is printed without a space. Possible printing errors left as printed: "quasi" for "quasi/quasi", "deniq;" and "obstrinxit" with the long s rendered as s. No tag for the stroke over "Tibi" in the scan was made. Note: the scan is slightly skewed; a few letters near the right margin are faint.
